log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Opponent is heavy on Steel/Dark/Ground with likely Incineroar lead. Incineroar gives Fake Out and Intimidate control, Primarina beats their Incineroar/Garchomp/Kingambit, Dragonite beats Garchomp and sweeps.

Incineroar's Intimidate and Fake Out blunt the opponent's physical attackers (Garchomp, Kingambit, Dragonite). Gholdengo adds strong special pressure that can hit Primarina and Incineroar. Kingambit gives a bulky Steel/Dark physical attacker that handles Dragonite and Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick three from my team of incineroar, garchomp, gholdengo, kingambit, sinistcha, archaludon against their garchomp, gholdengo, incineroar, primarina, dragonite, kingambit. Incineroar seems like a strong lead with intimidate and fake out, especially against their physical threats like garchomp and kingambit, while I'm weighing how to handle their primarina and dragonite.

Gholdengo pairs well as a special attacker since steel resists several of their threats, and kingambit gives me a solid dark/steel presence against garchomp. I'll settle on incineroar, gholdengo, and kingambit as my core three, keeping things straightforward rather than overanalyzing archaludon's weaknesses to fire and ground.

decisions.thought: Both sides lead Incineroar, and ours is faster (80 vs 60 base Speed). Fake Out is legal on the first turn and flinches the opponent's Incineroar before it can act. Flare Blitz is resisted by the Fire typing.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: I'm considering turn 1 options with both Incineroar on the field—Fake Out for a neutral-damage flinch versus Flare Blitz, which would be resisted since the opponent is also Fire/Dark type.

decisions.thought: Mirror Incineroar lead is a speed mindgame on Fake Out. Parting Shot avoids the tie and pivots to a better matchup while dropping their offenses.
Mirror Incineroar is slower than mine, so Parting Shot will drop its offenses and pivot out safely before it attacks.

We outspeed the opposing Incineroar (80 vs 60), and both sides are at -1 Attack. Flare Blitz is our strongest damage option and should take a large chunk of their 91% HP, with Sitrus Berry as backup. Parting Shot would just pivot into a Fire-weak Steel type.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm comparing both Incineroar's stats with Intimidate dropping each at -1 attack, trying to estimate how much damage a Flare Blitz would deal given the opponent's 91% HP and unclear HP stat.

Parting Shot seems like a promising option here too, since it would drop their attack further to -2 while pivoting us out to Gholdengo or Kingambit—though both are weak to Fire, which gives me pause since Flare Blitz is fire-typed. I'm also weighing our Incineroar's speed against theirs to figure out who acts first if we trade Flare Blitz hits.

decisions.thought: Opponent Incineroar is at -2 Attack and walled, so Primarina resists its STABs and threatens a knockout while covering their Garchomp and Kingambit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating forced switch options between primarina and dragonite against opponent Incineroar and bench threats.

decisions.thought: Primarina outspeeds Incineroar and Sparkling Aria is super-effective with Mystic Water boost, so it should knock out the weakened Incineroar.

Our Incineroar is at -2 Attack and -1 Special Attack, and Flare Blitz is not very effective into Primarina. Gholdengo resists Fairy, outspeeds Primarina (136 vs 60), and its Make It Rain is 2x super effective on Primarina, so it can threaten a knockout next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar's stats down, I'm weighing the matchup against Primarina—its Flare Blitz isn't great against Water, and Primarina's STAB moves threaten Incineroar hard since Fairy hits Dark super-effectively.

I'm considering switching to Kingambit instead, checking whether Steel/Dark typing gives it better defensive coverage against Primarina's Fairy/Water STABs, and whether Kowtow Cleave would be a strong response.

Checking the numbers, Kingambit outspeeds Primarina and hits decently hard with Iron Head given Primarina's weak defense, while its solid special bulk should let it tank Primarina's special attacks reasonably well.

Gholdengo could also be a good switch-in since Steel doesn't resist or get hit hard by Water, and its Make It Rain would punish Primarina's Fairy typing, though I need to double check how Fairy-type attacks actually interact with Steel defensively.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is at 23% and Primarina's STAB Sparkling Aria will finish it if it stays. Primarina is slower but bulky enough to take a hit first.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing turn order and damage to choose between Sparkling Aria and Flip Turn for a KO.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is much faster than Primarina (136 vs 60 base Speed), so it should move first. Thunderbolt is 2x super effective against Water/Fairy and hits harder than the resisted Make It Rain, which should knock Primarina out before it can use Sparkling Aria.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Gholdengo is down to 38 HP against a full-health Primarina, but speed favors me at 136 versus Primarina's 60, so I should move first. Primarina's Sparkling Aria hits hard with that 126 base SpA, and against my Steel/Ghost typing it's just neutral damage, so I need to weigh whether my special defense of 111 can tank a hit if I don't knock it out first.

Thunderbolt looks like the right call — Electric is super effective against Primarina's Water typing and isn't resisted by Fairy, so with my 203 SpA and Life Orb boost this should be a likely OHKO even without STAB.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo fainted, so I must switch. Primarina is at 18% and slower than Kingambit (102 vs 60), so Kingambit switches in and can attack first. Its Steel-type Iron Head is super effective against Water/Fairy and should finish Primarina.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Gholdengo fainted, so I need to switch between Incineroar and Kingambit. With Primarina at 18% HP, I'm weighing whether Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing gives it a favorable matchup against Water/Fairy, since Dark hits Fairy super effectively while Steel is neutral to Water.

decisions.thought: Primarina is at 18% HP and is weak to Dark, so Kowtow Cleave should knock it out. Kingambit's Attack is huge and Primarina is slower, so the hit should land first. Kowtow's damage beats Sucker Punch here, and Sucker Punch would fail anyway since Primarina attacks with a special move.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Primarina at 18% HP is in trouble against Kingambit, who outspeeds it and has Kowtow Cleave, a Dark-type move that's super effective against the Fairy typing. Even without priority, Kingambit moves first due to its superior speed, and Sucker Punch would also finish the job if needed.

decisions.thought: Primarina at 18% will die to any Kingambit attack like Sucker Punch, so staying in is lost. Flip Turn lets me chip then pivot safely into Intimidate.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Primarina's turn-one move versus Kingambit's type matchup and speed advantage under legal switch constraints.

decisions.thought: Opponent Kingambit is a physical Dark attacker, so switching in Intimidate Incineroar weakens Kowtow Cleave and resists Dark while preserving Dragonite's Multiscale.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating a competitive Pokémon switch between Incineroar and Dragonite against Kingambit given HP and ability matchups.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is at -1 Attack and every attacking option is resisted by the Fire/Dark Incineroar, so none will knock it out. Swords Dance brings Attack back to +1 and keeps Kingambit in to threaten a real hit later. The opponent's Parting Shot is the main risk, but attacking now only gets resisted damage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is down with -1 attack, and Incineroar sits at 71% HP. Since Incineroar is Fire/Dark, a Dark-type move from Kingambit gets resisted by its Dark typing, landing at 0.5x damage.

Iron Head only hits 0.5x too against Fire, and Sucker Punch suffers the same Dark resistance. Given the weakened attacking options, Swords Dance seems like a solid play to restore attack to +1 instead of forcing a weak hit, though I need to weigh the risk of a Flare Blitz coming in super-effectively against Kingambit's Steel typing.

decisions.thought: Kingambit threatens setup or strong Dark STAB, and Incineroar is faster. Fake Out has highest priority to flinch it for free and block any move this turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Incineroar options against Kingambit and choosing Parting Shot for a safe pivot to Dragonite.

decisions.thought: Incineroar outspeeds Kingambit (80 vs 50) and Flare Blitz is super effective vs Dark/Steel, so it should knock out before taking another resisted Kowtow.

Incineroar is Fire/Dark, so my Dark and Steel attacks are all resisted. Kowtow Cleave has the highest base power and the most damage output among them, and it is not priority, so it does not depend on the opponent attacking first. Switching to my Incineroar would not gain much here.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the type matchups here—our Kingambit took a stat drop from Incineroar's intimidate, and I'm working out why Kowtow Cleave was resisted earlier against Primarina, since Dark is not very effective against Fairy-types.

Steel moves also get resisted by Incineroar's Fire typing, so both Iron Head and Sucker Punch would deal reduced damage, while their Fire attacks hit our Steel typing hard. I notice only Incineroar is listed as a legal switch option, which seems odd since Garchomp should be available too, but I'll work with the legal choices given—weighing Sucker Punch's accuracy and power against Kowtow Cleave's guaranteed hit.

decisions.thought: Kingambit has fainted, and the only legal action is switching in Incineroar. I must choose that switch.
Mirror Incineroar at 48% with -1 Attack loses the Flare Blitz trade, so Parting Shot to pivot into Dragonite preserves momentum.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating the optimal move by comparing speed, attack penalty, and available switch options for the Incineroar matchup.

decisions.thought: Their Incineroar is at 48% with Sitrus Berry already used, and Fake Out will fail since ours has been active for a while. Parting Shot lowers their Attack again and brings in Garchomp, who is faster and threatens a Earthquake knockout next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Our Incineroar is at 189/202 HP while the opponent's sits at 48% and has lost its Sitrus Berry already, whereas ours still has that cushion. Speed-wise ours should outpace theirs given the base stat difference, so I'm leaning toward going with Flare Blitz here to capitalize on the speed and damage advantage.

Checking Fake Out too: 40 BP Normal-type priority move does roughly 47 damage, not enough to KO, and it only works on the first turn their Incineroar is out anyway.

Flare Blitz hits for about 68, taking them from 48% to roughly 29 HP, though recoil hurts us too. Alternatively, Parting Shot would drop their attack further and let us pivot to Garchomp, whose Earthquake hits Incineroar for 2x since it's Fire/Dark — that could be the cleaner finish.

Fire resisted by Garchomp's dragon typing, so damage is manageable. Garchomp outspeeds their Incineroar and can Earthquake next turn for a likely KO since ground hits hard against it, plus Parting Shot's attack drop softens any Flare Blitz they throw out.

decisions.thought: Only legal action is switching to Dragonite, so I must take it to reset Intimidate drops.
Dragonite has full HP Multiscale to tank any hit, and Incineroar is at -1 Attack. Setting up Dragon Dance now wins speed and power for a sweep.

Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragonite and Incineroar is already at -1 Attack, so it would do little and cost recoil. Parting Shot lowers Dragonite's Attack and Special Attack and lets me switch into Garchomp, which outspeeds it and hits hard with Outrage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 189/202 HP with -1 attack and -1 special attack, facing a full-health Dragonite with unknown item, possibly holding Multiscale-boosting ability at full HP. I'm weighing whether Flare Blitz is still worth using given my lowered attack and Dragon's resistance to Fire-type moves.

Parting Shot looks like the better play here since it drops Dragonite's attack and special attack while letting me switch to Garchomp, which outspeeds Dragonite and could threaten with Outrage. Comparing my three legal options -- Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Protect -- I'm leaning toward Parting Shot since it offers tempo advantage by debuffing the opponent while setting up a stronger matchup.

decisions.thought: Opponent Incineroar is at -1 and can't threaten Multiscale Dragonite, and my +1 Attack was cancelled by Parting Shot. Re-using Dragon Dance restores offensive pressure while staying faster than their whole unrevealed bench. Earthquake or Ice Punch now would be weak without a boost.

Dragonite's Dragon Dance is already partly cancelled by our earlier Parting Shot. Another Parting Shot drops its Attack to -1 and Special Attack to -2 while Incineroar pivots out, so Garchomp can come in and hit it with a 2x Outrage. Flare Blitz only does moderate damage and costs recoil.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 189/202 with -1 Attack and -1 Special Attack. The opponent's Dragonite used Dragon Dance then Parting Shot, netting it +1 Speed but -1 Attack and -1 Special Attack overall, and with base Speed 80 tied to mine, that boost likely lets it move first.

Considering options: Flare Blitz only hits Dragonite for 0.5x since Fire is resisted by Dragon-types, and with my lowered Attack it wouldn't do much damage. Parting Shot again would stack more debuffs on Dragonite and let me switch into Garchomp, which at full HP outspeeds the boosted Dragonite and can land a crushing super-effective Outrage since Dragon-type STAB hits Dragonite for 2x and Ground-type Earthquake would be useless against its Flying typing anyway.

Since switching isn't directly listed among legal actions, I'll go with Parting Shot, which further cripples Dragonite's attack and special attack while pivoting me out into a better position.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is at +2 Speed with Multiscale intact and outspeeds Incineroar, so the Parting Shot loop must be punished with damage now.

Dragonite's net Attack is at 0 after our repeated Parting Shots, but it has +2 Speed. Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon-types and won't threaten a knockout. Parting Shot lowers its Attack again and brings in a better answer, Garchomp, who outspeeds it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Tracking the stat changes on Dragonite: two Dragon Dances boost attack and speed, but Incineroar's repeated Parting Shot each turn has been cutting its attack and special attack back down, so I'm trying to work out the net attack stage after these interactions.

Fire from Flare Blitz hits Dragonite for resisted damage since Dragon resists Fire, so I'm looking at whether another Parting Shot to further tank its offenses and pivot to Garchomp, Archaludon, or Sinistcha is the better line than attacking directly.

decisions.thought:
Dragonite is faster at +2 Speed and Earthquake already dropped Incineroar to Sitrus range, so a second Earthquake should knock it out if it stays.
Staying aggressive beats another Parting Shot cycle.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing battle state and type matchups to evaluate Earthquake versus a likely Sinistcha switch and alternative moves.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is already at -3 SpA, so Parting Shot's real value is cutting its Attack again and forcing a switch. Earthquake would hit my Incineroar super effectively, so I should not stay in and trade. Parting Shot brings in Garchomp, which resists nothing relevant but is immune to nothing Dragonite has, yet Outrage hits Dragonite hard and Dragonite's Earthquake does nothing to Flying types.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite's boosted speed means it outpaces our Incineroar, and with Parting Shot already lowering our stats, Earthquake would hit Incineroar hard since it's part Dark but neutral to ground, actually just normal damage since Fire/Dark isn't weak to ground.

Flare Blitz back on Dragonite would deal moderate but not lethal damage given Dragonite's bulk and the fire-resist-adjacent typing. I'm weighing whether another Parting Shot to chip Dragonite's stats further and pivot to Garchomp makes sense, since Garchomp's dragon/ground typing would take Earthquake only neutrally.

Garchomp also outpaces Dragonite even with its boosted speed and threatens back with Outrage for heavy damage, so switching Incineroar out via Parting Shot while bringing in Garchomp looks like the safer, more aggressive play here.

decisions.thought: Opponent Incineroar is at 9% and will likely Parting Shot again or switch out. Dragonite is faster but ExtremeSpeed gives priority to guarantee the KO before any move.

Dragonite is at +2 Speed, so it outspeeds Incineroar and will Earthquake before Parting Shot or Flare Blitz can resolve. Only Protect guarantees Incineroar survives this turn, and it can then use Parting Shot next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar at 19 HP and Dragonite now outspeeding thanks to its +2 boost, Earthquake would knock it out first if Dragonite targets it, and even Flare Blitz wouldn't score a clean KO on full-health Dragonite since Fire resists Dragon.

Parting Shot looks like the right call here - it drops Dragonite's Attack further while pulling Incineroar out safely to a healthy teammate like Sinistcha, Archaludon, or Garchomp, since Gholdengo and Kingambit are already down. I'm weighing Garchomp as the switch-in since its Flying typing on Dragonite doesn't matter but Garchomp itself resists nothing special from Earthquake - it's just about avoiding the Fire-vs-Ground 2x weakness that doomed Incineroar.

But checking speed: Dragonite with its Dragon Dance boost is actually faster than Incineroar, so if I go Parting Shot, Dragonite moves first and Incineroar dies to Earthquake before it even gets to execute the switch. That changes everything - Protect is actually the only move that keeps Incineroar alive this turn, even though it's just a stall. I'm settling on Protect.

decisions.thought: Opponent Incineroar is at 9% HP, so priority Extreme Speed guarantees the knockout before Parting Shot or Flare Blitz.

Dragonite is faster and will likely KO the 19 HP Incineroar before it moves, so Protect is the only way to survive this turn. But Protect was used last turn, so it may fail. Parting Shot still has the most value: Dragonite's Attack and Special Attack are already crippled, and it lets Incineroar switch out.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar sitting at 19 HP is doomed to almost anything, while Dragonite is at full health with a speed boost making it much faster despite the attack and special attack drops. I'm checking whether Dragonite can safely finish things off given its speed advantage and Incineroar's weakened offense.

Another Parting Shot would drop Dragonite's stats further and bring in a fresh teammate like Garchomp, Archaludon, or Sinistcha, so I'm weighing whether that pivot actually helps against Dragonite's typing given Earthquake's neutral matchup against Garchomp's Dragon/Ground typing.

Since Dragonite is faster, it could use Extreme Speed to KO Incineroar before Parting Shot resolves, which makes Protect the safer option -- it blocks the hit this turn even though it only delays the inevitable switch.

Dragonite's already boosted with Dragon Dance and attacking, so Protect risks failing from consecutive use while Parting Shot keeps its value regardless of what Dragonite does. I'll go with Parting Shot.
